test_cases.description: Running the migration against an existing database that lacks the new columns adds workspace_mode, upstream_url, and integration_branch columns, and existing rows read back with correct defaults.
preconditions: SQLite database file exists with a workspaces table that does NOT have workspace_mode, upstream_url, or integration_branch columns
At least one existing workspace row is present in the table
Hub migration function is available
test_cases.input: Call the database migration function against the existing database
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: err = runMigration(db); assert err == nil; row = db.QueryRow('SELECT workspace_mode, upstream_url, integration_branch FROM workspaces WHERE slug = existing_slug'); assert row.workspace_mode == 'standard'; assert row.upstream_url == NULL; assert row.integration_branch == NULL

test_cases.description: Initializing schema against a fresh empty database creates the workspaces table with all three new columns present without requiring ALTER TABLE.
preconditions: Fresh empty SQLite database file (no tables)
Hub schema initializer function is available
test_cases.input: Call the schema initializer against the empty database
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: err = initSchema(db); assert err == nil; cols = db.QueryRow('PRAGMA table_info(workspaces)'); assert cols contains 'workspace_mode'; assert cols contains 'upstream_url'; assert cols contains 'integration_branch'

test_cases.description: Inserting a workspace row without specifying workspace_mode stores 'standard' as the default, and inserting with workspace_mode=NULL is rejected by the database constraint.
preconditions: SQLite database initialized with the updated workspaces schema including workspace_mode NOT NULL DEFAULT 'standard'

input.case_a: INSERT INTO workspaces omitting workspace_mode column
input.case_b: INSERT INTO workspaces with workspace_mode = NULL

expected.case_a: Row inserted successfully; SELECT workspace_mode returns 'standard'
expected.case_b: Database returns a NOT NULL constraint violation error

test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: // Case A: err = db.Exec('INSERT INTO workspaces (slug, ...) VALUES (?, ...)', 'test-slug', ...); assert err == nil; row = db.QueryRow('SELECT workspace_mode FROM workspaces WHERE slug = ?', 'test-slug'); assert row.workspace_mode == 'standard'; // Case B: err = db.Exec('INSERT INTO workspaces (slug, workspace_mode, ...) VALUES (?, NULL, ...)', 'test-slug2', ...); assert err != nil; assert err contains 'NOT NULL constraint'

test_cases.description: When a carry_patch workspace clone job executes, it clones git_url as origin, adds 'upstream' remote, sets rerere config, and creates the integration branch, then marks clone_status as 'ready'.
preconditions: Hub server is running with initialized SQLite database
A carry_patch workspace with git_url, upstream_url='https://github.com/upstream/repo.git', integration_branch='deploy' exists with clone_status='pending'
GitRunner with RemoteAdd, ConfigSet, CreateBranch methods is available (mocked)
go-git PlainCloneContext is available (mocked)
test_cases.input: Clone job is dequeued and executed for the carry_patch workspace

expected.integration_branch_created: deploy branch at upstream tracking HEAD

test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: executeCloneJob(workspaceSlug); ws = db.QueryRow('SELECT clone_status FROM workspaces WHERE slug = ?', workspaceSlug); assert ws.clone_status == 'ready'; assert mockGitRunner.RemoteAddCalled with ('upstream', upstream_url); assert mockGitRunner.ConfigSetCalled with ('rerere.enabled', 'true'); assert mockGitRunner.ConfigSetCalled with ('rerere.autoupdate', 'true'); assert mockGitRunner.CreateBranchCalled with ('deploy', upstreamTrackingHEAD)

test_cases.description: When a post-clone setup step (e.g., RemoteAdd) fails after the core clone succeeds, the workspace is still marked 'ready' and a warning is logged.
preconditions: A carry_patch workspace clone job is about to execute
go-git PlainCloneContext succeeds
GitRunner.RemoteAdd is configured to return an error
test_cases.input: Clone job executes; RemoteAdd returns error 'connection refused'
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: mockGitRunner.RemoteAdd = func() error { return errors.New('connection refused') }; err = executeCloneJob(workspaceSlug); assert err == nil; ws = db.QueryRow('SELECT clone_status FROM workspaces WHERE slug = ?', workspaceSlug); assert ws.clone_status == 'ready'; assert logBuffer contains 'warning' or 'warn'

test_cases.description: When a standard workspace clone job executes, no upstream remote is added, no rerere config is set, and no integration branch is created.
preconditions: A standard workspace clone job is about to execute
go-git PlainCloneContext is available (mocked)
GitRunner methods are available (mocked and call-tracked)
test_cases.input: Clone job executes for a workspace with workspace_mode='standard'
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: executeCloneJob(standardWorkspaceSlug); assert mockGitRunner.RemoteAddCallCount == 0; assert mockGitRunner.ConfigSetCallCount == 0; assert mockGitRunner.CreateBranchCallCount == 0; ws = db.QueryRow('SELECT clone_status FROM workspaces WHERE slug = ?', standardWorkspaceSlug); assert ws.clone_status == 'ready'

property_tests.description: For any sequence of add, remove, and update-position operations on a carry_patch workspace, the set of position values is always exactly {1, 2, ..., N} with no gaps and no duplicates.

property_tests.description: For any carry_patch workspace, no two patches ever share the same (workspace_slug, branch_name) pair.

property_tests.description: For any carry_patch workspace with a defined integration_branch, no patch in the patches table ever has branch_name equal to the workspace's integration_branch.

property_tests.description: For any workspace with workspace_mode='carry_patch', upstream_url is always non-null and non-empty in the workspaces table.

property_tests.description: For any workspace that has been deleted, the patches table contains no rows with workspace_slug equal to the deleted workspace's slug.

property_tests.description: For any reorder operation on a workspace with N patches, after a successful reorder the workspace still has exactly N patches with positions {1, 2, ..., N}.
